Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x} & ⇒ & v=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2x}-\int \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2x}\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}3x{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{2x}\,{|}_{0}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}x{e}^{2x}\,{|}_{0}^{2}-\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2x}\,{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}(2\cdot {e}^{4}-0\cdot {e}^{0})-\frac{3}{4}({e}^{4}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =3{e}^{4}-\frac{3}{4}({e}^{4}-1) \\  & =\frac{9{e}^{4}+3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
